kb_proposals: LiftPropOn G.IsLocalStructomorphWithinAt is best handled through the forward local form (chartAt (f x) ∘ f = e ∘ chartAt x on an open set, CBG/FromModel RepOn, liftPropOn_iff_repOn): no chart symm is evaluated, so composition, inverse and rigidity become set-level arguments; mathlib has no general composition lemma for LiftPropOn.

Chart changes for local structomorphisms: StructureGroupoid.LocalInvariantProp.liftPropOn_indep_chart / liftPropWithinAt_indep_chart (any maximal-atlas charts) is the tool, as in mathlib's HasGroupoid.comp. CBG/FromModel liftPropOn_of_maximalAtlas_rep (a map that reads as one element of G in maximal-atlas charts κ, κ' on an open set is a morphism there) is a DIFFERENT statement from mathlib's homonym-trap StructureGroupoid.LocalInvariantProp.liftPropOn_of_mem_maximalAtlas (a maximal-atlas chart is a morphism on its source), not its converse; the CBG lemma was renamed from that name to avoid the kb/0016-style trap.

A charted space on an open subset of a Level-B structure is mathlib's TopologicalSpace.Opens.instChartedSpace with Opens.instHasGroupoid (ClosedUnderRestriction); corestriction is liftPropWithinAt_subtypeVal_comp_iff, rfl on the chart side.

INTERFACE NEEDS (Geometry.lean not edited): (1) A3 past side at BTZ points: Level B lacks B2 for a connected open regular set adherent to a singular point. A SUFFICIENT CANDIDATE, LIKELY FALSE AS STATED IN E₀ (so NOT to be added: LocalModel would lose its E₀ instance, kb/0011/0012): `localUnique_sing_adherent : ∀ U : Set Y, IsOpen U → IsConnected U → U ⊆ regY → ∀ y₀ ∈ closure U, ∀ α₀, 0 ≤ α₀ → y₀ ∈ singY α₀ → ∀ z₀ ∈ singY α₀, ∀ f : Y → Y, (∀ y ∈ U, G.IsLocalStructomorphWithinAt f U y) → InjOn f U → MapsTo f U (connectedComponent y₀) → MapClusterPt z₀ (𝓝[U] y₀) f → ∃ e ∈ G, connectedComponent y₀ ⊆ e.source ∧ EqOn f e U`. The cluster hypothesis is NECESSARY (by hand, not formalized: without it a small Minkowski rotation of a regular ball adherent to the BTZ line, moving the contact point off the line, is an injective G-morphism into the model that is the restriction of no element of Isom(E₀)). It is NOT SUFFICIENT (audit counterexample, by hand, not formalized): in E₀ = (open half-space bounded by the null plane Δ^⊥)/⟨P⟩ ∪ Δ take U a thin open cone in reg(E₀) with vertex y₀ ∈ Δ and axis v transverse to Δ (it lifts to a cone at D(y₀) disjoint from its P^n-translates, P^n v ≠ v), and g ∈ SO(1,2) a small rotation fixing D(y₀) outside the (about 1-dimensional) normalizer of ⟨P⟩; then f = π∘g∘lift is an injective local G-structomorphism on the connected regular open U, maps into the component of y₀, and f(u) → y₀ ∈ sing₀, so the cluster hypothesis holds with z₀ = y₀; yet by B1 any e ∈ Isom(E₀) restricting to f would lift to g modulo deck transformations, which g is not. A point-contact piece is too small. The true past-side field needs a LARGENESS hypothesis on the connected regular piece near y₀ — for example that it has the form reg(U'') ∩ I⁻_{U''}(r), or that every neighbourhood of y₀ meets it in a set whose closure contains a segment of y₀'s line. Its exact form is gx's to fix (it is the 'past-side B2 step outside U' that A3-B-INVESTIGATION.md says gx owes). (2) A3 otherwise needs no new Level B field, but needs packages 2 (causal convexity) and 5 (Prop 3.7, K± at BTZ points) and lem:Sigma_separe (no field of Geometry/LocalModel; package 5's interface need): it is not a pure Level B→A derivation, so its natural home is package 5/6 or the instance, with the B2 step from here (exists_eqOn_of_connected_reg/_sing, exists_extension_of_eqOn). (3) A4 is Sbierski Thm 3.6's slice construction, package 6 content; B4 provides only the local τ. Whether B4 suffices (its level sets are Cauchy in SOME GH N ⊆ W, nothing ties N to the future of the maximum level) is not settled here. (4) Design risk 'connectedness of D ∩ V': confirmed real for A3 (U ∩ W need not be connected); the connected piece is U ∩ W ∩ J⁺_W(r) and its connectedness is causal, not chart-level. For A4 there is no ψ, hence no connectedness issue inside A4 itself (it reappears in Thm 3.6's ψ = φ on N ∩ U, package 6).
